selection_note: These 11 illustrations were curated after unblinding from the frozen challenger-stratified confirmation review: 46 text and 15 photo cases, including agreements and all five revised-guide photo disagreements. The sample is not representative of population accuracy or balanced between designs. Reviewers saw anonymous A/B assignments and each pair’s own full catalog; notes were sealed before identities were revealed. Their exact model identity is unknown, their compute is outside the experiment API ledger, and their judgments are fallible. One text case has apparently transposed rationales; its sealed bytes and counts remain preserved, but it is excluded from these illustrations. No replacement review or further tuning followed confirmation.

cases.summary: The revised guide explicitly includes social conversation, yet Decisions rejects this greeting as Other. The blinded reviewer supports Sol and calls the rejection unsupported. The original guide is less explicit, and its choices were judged plausible.

Decisions changes from the shared Assistant choice to Other. The reviewer calls this a clear rejection error: asking about the assistant’s pets concerns its background. Both guides retain background scope, so this is not evidence that the rewrite forgot it.

A reference-model error: the reviewer supports Decisions’ Knowledge choice and calls revised-guide Sol’s Assistant choice unsupported. Learning how to say a greeting differs from greeting the assistant. The original pair agrees on Knowledge.

Both guides leave a reasonable ambiguity: the battery could belong to a car or another device. The reviewer considers Sol’s vehicle-care interpretation and Decisions’ Other plausible, rather than treating either as an obvious error.

A 401k rollover crosses financial transfers and employee benefits. The reviewer supports both revised-guide choices despite their disagreement. The original pair agrees on employee benefits; agreement alone cannot resolve the overlapping scope.

An improved agreement example: both revised-guide classifiers select Money & Banking and receive supported judgments. The original Decisions rejection was judged unsupported. “Visa card” supplies the banking cue, rather than an immigration-visa request.

One of three changed Sol photo assignments: a sand sculptor moves from shared People to Sol Other. The reviewer prefers Decisions’ People choice, while allowing an artwork-centered Other reading as plausible.
cases.alt: A person kneels beside sand sculptures of human figures while a crowd watches.

cases.summary: Another changed Sol assignment: industrial equipment moves from shared Other to Sol Electronics. The reviewer prefers Decisions’ Other because the guide specifies household or desktop devices, while considering Sol plausible. On the preselected repeat, Sol returns to Other.
cases.alt: An industrial compressor, motor, tank and piping stand against an interior brick wall.

cases.summary: The remaining changed Sol assignment: engines on a trailer move from shared Vehicles to Sol Other. Both readings were judged plausible because detached mechanical parts dominate a vehicle setting. Decisions’ prediction stays Vehicles.
cases.alt: Detached engines and mechanical assemblies fill a wheeled trailer, with cars and trucks behind it.

cases.summary: This occupied assembly hall supports both People and Buildings under both guides. The reviewer supports both focal interpretations. A disagreement can reflect competing subjects within one photograph.
cases.alt: A wide view of a curved assembly chamber filled with seated people, desks and galleries.

cases.summary: A shared Other check: both classifiers reject this volcanic landscape under both guides, and all four judgments are supported. A missing landscape category makes rejection reasonable; shared rejection still does not establish broad semantic accuracy.
cases.alt: A large bare volcanic mountain rises above green vegetation under a pale sky.
